extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry and Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal definitions and functorial properties for bridges, capsules, processions, and Hodge-theaters (Θ±, Θell, Θ±ell, Θ±ellNF) in the context of IUT; includes symmetry/indeterminacy statements and functorial constructions. Targeted at constructing and relating these objects via functorial algorithms and gluing isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-Θell-Bridge functor and F±_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of associating to a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater the underlying D-Θell-bridge determines a natural functor (category of D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters → category of D-Θell-bridges) whose output data admits an F±_l-symmetry — i.e., a symmetry given by the action of a finite group equipped with a natural outer isomorphism to F±_l — which acts doubly transitively (transitively with stabilizers of order two) on the index set (“T”) of the underlying capsule of D-prime-strips (“†DT”) of this output data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a structural requirement: the forgetful functor must produce output carrying an F±_l-action with the stated double-transitivity on capsule indices; see Proposition 6.8(i) and cross-reference Proposition 6.6(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic Capsules functor and Sl±-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of associating to a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater its l±-capsule †D|T| (associated to the underlying D-Θ±-bridge) determines a natural functor (category of D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters → category of l±-capsules of D-prime-strips) whose output data admits an Sl±-symmetry (symmetric group on l± letters) which acts transitively on the index set |T|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functor effectively 'forgets the labels ∈ |Fl| = Fl/{±1}' (i.e., the bijection |T| ∼→ |Fl| determined by the F±_l-group structure). Consequently, if one is only given the output †D|T| up to isomorphism, there are precisely l± possibilities for which element ∈ |Fl| a given index |t| ∈ |T| corresponds to prior to applying the functor. See Proposition 6.8(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Capsules functor
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing the functor of holomorphic capsules with the mono-analyticization operation yields a natural functor to l±-capsules of D^(cid:4)-prime-strips whose output data satisfies the same symmetry properties with respect to labels as the functor of (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures mono-analyticized output preserves the same label-symmetry behavior; see Proposition 6.8(iii) and Definition 4.1(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic Processions functor and label-indeterminacy reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ±-bridge †φΘ± : †DT → †D, the assignment †φΘ± → Prc(†DT) (the l±-procession of D-prime-strips determined by appropriate subcapsules) determines a natural functor (category of D-Θ±-bridges → category of processions of D-prime-strips) whose output satisfies: for each n ∈ {1,...,l±} there are precisely n possibilities for the element ∈ |Fl| to which a given index of the index set of the n-capsule corresponds prior to applying the functor. By taking products over |Fl|, considering processions reduces the indeterminacy from (l±)^(l±) to a total of l±! possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functor organizes capsule data into processions thereby drastically reducing label-indeterminacy; see Proposition 6.9(i) and Fig. 6.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Processions functor
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing the holomorphic-processions functor with mono-analyticization yields a natural functor to processions of D^(cid:4)-prime-strips whose output data satisfies the same indeterminacy properties with respect to labels as the holomorphic procession functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same preservation-of-indeterminacy property after mono-analyticization; see Proposition 6.9(ii) and Definition 4.1(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of procession functors with earlier functors
rubrics_metrics.description: The functors of (i) and (ii) (processions and mono-analytic processions) are compatible with the functors of Proposition 4.11 (i),(ii) relative to the functor determined by the functorial algorithm of Proposition 6.7: natural inclusions S_j → S_t determine natural transformations between the respective composites and the procession functors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility is expressed by natural transformations determined by the inclusions S_j = {1,...,j} ↪ S_t = {0,...,t−1}; see Proposition 6.9(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite functor to D^(cid:4)-prime-strips and the base-Θ±ell link
rubrics_metrics.description: The composite functor (from category of D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters to category of D^(cid:4)-prime-strips) obtained by assigning to a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater the mono-analyticization †D^(cid:4)> of the D-prime-strip associated via the functorial algorithm of Proposition 6.7 defines, for two D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters †HT and ‡HT, the base-Θ±ell- (or D-Θ±ell-) link D−→ between them to be the full poly-isomorphism †D^(cid:4)> ∼→ ‡D^(cid:4)> produced by this functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This furnishes a notion of link between Hodge theaters via the mono-analyticized D-prime-strips; see Corollary 6.10(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic core (constant invariant) for infinite linked chains
rubrics_metrics.description: If one has an infinite chain ... D−→ (n−1)HT → nHT → (n+1)HT ... of D-Θ±ell-linked D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters, then applying the composite functor of (i) yields a resulting chain of full poly-isomorphisms between the D^(cid:4)-prime-strips; the output data forms a constant invariant — i.e., a mono-analytic core — of the infinite chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies a central mono-analytic object invariant under the infinite linkage; see Corollary 6.10(ii) and Remark 3.8.1(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Etale-picture diagram admits permutation symmetries among spokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewing each D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater in the infinite chain as a spoke emanating from the mono-analytic core yields an ´etale-picture diagram whose construction admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (i.e., among the labels n ∈ Z of the D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identification of mono-analyticized zero-labeled D-prime-strips across spokes yields multiple holomorphic structures on the core; see Corollary 6.10(iii) and Fig. 6.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Θ±-bridge (structure and lifting condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θ±-bridge (relative to given initial Θ-data) is a polymorphism †ψΘ± : †FT → †F (†F a F-prime-strip), where T is an F±_l-group and †FT = {†Ft}_t∈T is a capsule of F-prime-strips indexed by T, that lifts a D-Θ±-bridge †φΘ± : †DT → †D. The l±-capsule †F|T| is formed from †FT by quotienting T by {±1} and identifying components in fibers via constituent poly-morphisms; each constituent F-prime-strip of †F|T| is only well-defined up to a positive automorphism (indeterminacy which does not affect applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphisms/isomorphisms of Θ±-bridges are defined as pairs of poly-isomorphisms †FT ∼→ ‡FT and †F ∼→ ‡F that lift a morphism between associated D-Θ±-bridges; composition is evident. See Definition 6.11(i) and cross-reference Definition 6.4(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Θell-bridge (torsor-indexed capsule and relation to D-Θell-bridge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θell-bridge (relative to given initial Θ-data) is †ψΘell : †FT → †D^(cid:6)± where †D^(cid:6)± is a category equivalent to D^(cid:6)±, T is an F±_l-torsor, and †FT = {†Ft}_t∈T is a capsule of F-prime-strips indexed by T; it is to be a D-Θell-bridge †φΘell : †DT → †D^(cid:6)± (†DT being the capsule of D-prime-strips associated to †FT). Morphisms/isomorphisms are pairs of poly-isomorphisms lifting associated D-Θell-bridges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the torsor-indexed analogue of Θ±-bridges; see Definition 6.11(ii) and Remark 5.2.1(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Θ±ell-Hodge theater (compatibility of Θ± and Θell pieces)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θ±ell-Hodge theater is a collection †HT Θ±ell = (†F, †ψΘ± ←− †FT, †ψΘell −→ †D^(cid:6)±) where †ψΘ± is a Θ±-bridge and †ψΘell is a Θell-bridge such that the associated data {†φΘ±, †φΘell} forms a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater. Morphisms/isomorphisms are pairs of morphisms between the respective associated Θ±- and Θell-bridges compatible so they induce the same poly-isomorphism between the capsules of F-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gluing/compatibility conditions ensure the underlying D-objects form a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater; see Definition 6.11(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijectivity of isomorphisms between Θ-bridges and associated D-bridges
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural functorially induced map from the set of isomorphisms between two Θ±-bridges (respectively Θell-bridges; Θ±ell-Hodge theaters) to the set of isomorphisms between the respective associated D-Θ±-bridges (resp. D-Θell-bridges; D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters) is bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphism classification of Θ-objects is controlled completely by associated D-objects; see Corollary 6.12(i) and Corollary 5.3(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsor structure for gluing Θ±- and Θell-bridges
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Θ±-bridge and a Θell-bridge, the set of capsule-+-full poly-isomorphisms between the respective capsules of F-prime-strips which allow gluing the given Θ±- and Θell-bridges to form a Θ±ell-Hodge theater forms a torsor over the group F±_l × {±1}^V. The first factor corresponds to induced isomorphisms of F±_l-torsors between index sets of the capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the parameter space (torsor) of possible gluing isomorphisms; see Corollary 6.12(ii) and Proposition 6.6(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithmic construction and lifting of Θ-bridge portions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 6.7 provides a functorial algorithm for constructing a D-Θ-bridge from a D-Θ±-bridge. If the constructed D-Θ-bridge arises as the D-Θ-bridge associated to a Θ-bridge whose portion '‡F_J → ‡F>' is completely determined by the associated D-Θ-bridge, then that portion may be regarded as constructed via a functorial algorithm similar to Proposition 6.7 from the Θ±-bridge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that the portion of Θ-bridges determined by D-bridges can be obtained functorially and that isomorphisms correspond bijectively; see Remark 6.12.2(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing Θ±ell-Hodge theater to ΘNF-Hodge theater via functorial algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Gluing a Θ±ell-Hodge theater to a ΘNF-Hodge theater along their associated Θ±- and Θ-bridges via the functorial algorithm of Proposition 6.7 yields a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater. The gluing isomorphism occurring in such a gluing operation is unique (by Proposition 4.8(ii); Corollary 5.6(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction allows mixing additive and multiplicative structures; see Remark 6.12.2(ii) and subsequent discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater and D-version
rubrics_metrics.description: A Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is a triple consisting of (a) a Θ±ell-Hodge theater, (b) a ΘNF-Hodge theater, and (c) the (necessarily unique) gluing isomorphism between them. Similarly, a D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater is the triple of the D-versions together with the unique gluing isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines additive (Θ±ell) and multiplicative (ΘNF) theories into a single object; see Definition 6.13(i),(ii) and Fig. 6.5 for combinatorial structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of F±_l and F2_l symmetries for networks of comparison isomorphisms without label-crushing
rubrics_metrics.description: Both F±_l- (additive) and F2_l- (multiplicative) symmetries are applied to establish explicit networks of comparison isomorphisms relating objects (e.g., log-volumes) associated to non-labeled prime-strips permuted by the symmetry; an important property is that these networks operate without 'label crushing' (i.e., they preserve bijective relationships between index sets and labels). This synchronization of labels stems from the single connected component/basepoint of the global object appearing in the Hodge theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains intended application of symmetries in building comparison isomorphisms and the crucial role of single basepoint connectivity; see Remark 6.12.4(i),(ii) and Remarks 4.9.1–4.9.2 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global ±-synchronization and inclusion of zero in F_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The F±_l-symmetry includes the zero element ∈ Fl, allowing the network of comparison isomorphisms to relate zero-labeled prime-strips to nonzero-labeled prime-strips in a 'combinatorially holomorphic' way compatible with bijections to global ±-label classes of cusps. However, this inclusion also prevents insulating nonzero-labeled prime-strips from confusion with the zero-labeled one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights a trade-off: ability to relate zero and nonzero labels vs. inability to isolate nonzero-labeled prime-strips; pertinent for later constructions (Gaussian Frobenioids, normalization of étale theta functions). See Remark 6.12.5(i)-(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric vs arithmetic nature of single basepoint for symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: For F±_l-symmetry (present §6) the 'single basepoint' is geometric: labels ∈ T correspond to collections of cusps in a single connected component of D_v at each v ∈ V and are permuted without permuting V±. By contrast, for F2_l-symmetry (§4) the single basepoint is arithmetic and the translations permute the subset V± in VBor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains suitability: F±_l-geometric basepoint is better for Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of the étale theta function, while F2_l-arithmetic basepoint suits construction of the number field Fmod. See Remark 6.12.6(i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial construction of label-bijections (†ζ, †ξ) from intrinsic structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The crucial bijections †ζ : LabCusp(†D^(cid:6)) ∼→ J and †ζ± : LabCusp±(†D^(cid:6)±) ∼→ T (and the †ξ's for global ±-synchronization) are constructed by means of functorial algorithms from the intrinsic structure of a D-Θ±ell- or D-ΘNF-Hodge theater — not by comparison with a fixed reference model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functoriality is essential for later combinations with log-shell theory and for preserving intrinsic nature of constructions; see Remark 6.12.4(iv) and references to Propositions 4.7(iii), 6.5(i)-(iii).
